sources.title: IRS releases tax inflation adjustments for tax year 2026

lines.say: Your first paycheck will be smaller than you think.
lines.show: Your first paycheck will be smaller than you think.

lines.say: Say you work twenty hours at fifteen dollars an hour. That's three hundred dollars.
lines.show: Say you work 20 hours at $15 an hour. That's $300.

lines.say: First, Social Security takes six point two percent. That's eighteen dollars and sixty cents.
Then Medicare takes one point four five percent. Another four dollars and thirty five cents.
So you keep two hundred seventy seven dollars and five cents, before any income tax.
lines.show: So you keep $277.05, before any income tax.

scenes.label: you can earn before federal income tax

lines.say: Good news. Earn under sixteen thousand one hundred dollars from a job this year, and you likely owe zero federal income tax.
lines.show: Good news. Earn under $16,100 from a job this year, and you likely owe $0 federal income tax.

lines.say: Check every pay stub. If income tax was withheld anyway, file a tax return to get it back.
lines.show: Check every pay stub. If income tax was withheld anyway, file a tax return to get it back.

lines.say: Social Security and Medicare don't come back as a refund.
lines.show: Social Security and Medicare don't come back as a refund.

scenes.takeaway: Know your pay stub before your first payday.
scenes.source: Data: SSA 2026 tax rates; IRS tax year 2026 adjustments
